claim: BIS's Cadence order covers 61 EAR violations: 56 unlicensed sales/loans to CSCC (NUDT alias), two charges for the actual and attempted transfer of CSCC items to Phytium, and three for software downloads by Entity-Listed JSC Mikron, Huawei and SMIC (2016-2021).
evidence: "alleges that Respondent committed 61 violations of the Regulations"; Charges 1-56 (CSCC), Charge 57 (transfer to Phytium), Charge 58 (attempted hardware transfer), "Charges 59-61 ... allowed Joint Stock Company Mikron (“Mikron”), Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. (“Huawei”), and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (“SMIC”) to continue making downloads" (BIS Order pp.1-7)

claim: BIS's July 2025 order requires Cadence to complete two internal audits of its export-control compliance programme, including oversight of Cadence China, covering 12-month periods from 1 September 2025 and 1 September 2026, with reports due 1 March 2027 and 1 March 2028.
evidence: "THIRD, Cadence shall complete two (2) internal audits of its export controls compliance program, including but not limited to its oversight over export controls compliance by Cadence China ... The first annual audit shall cover the 12-month period beginning on September 1, 2025 ... due ... no later than March 1, 2027. The second ... beginning on September 1, 2026 ... no later than March 1, 2028." (BIS Order pp.17-18)
notes: The order does not require independent or third-party auditors; the DLA Piper summary's 'third-party' wording is not in the primary text.

claim: On 24 September 2026 US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US-China 'Busan Agreement' trade truce, due to end on 10 November 2026, would be extended to 10 January 2027.
evidence: "We will extend what we call the 'Busan Agreement' — the economic détente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on Nov. 10 — that is going to be extended until Jan. 10," Bessent said in a Fox News Channel interview. (Quartz, 24 Sep 2026)

claim: Crowell & Moring reported on 30 September 2026 that the truce extension pushes back the BIS affiliates rule's return from 9 November 2026, but BIS had not yet published a Federal Register notice formally extending the suspension.
evidence: "The extension correspondingly pushes back the effective date of the BIS Affiliates Rule, which had been scheduled to go back into effect on November 9, 2026. As of the date of this writing, BIS has not yet published a Federal Register notice formally extending the suspension by two months." (Crowell & Moring, 30 Sep 2026)
notes: Updates CLM-1506 / CLM-0306: the 9 Nov 2026 expiry is expected to move, but this is not yet formalised. Re-check the Federal Register.
